items.followUp: Define one mole and give an example of one mole of oxygen molecules.

rubric.why: The number of entities in one mole is Avogadro’s number.
rubric.description: States the number of elementary entities in one mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving Avogadro’s number.

rubric.why: A correct example shows how a mole applies to a specific substance.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of one mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as one mole of carbon atoms.

modelAnswer: A mole is the amount of substance that contains 6.02 × 10²³ elementary entities, such as atoms, molecules or ions.
For example, 1 mol of carbon atoms contains 6.02 × 10²³ carbon atoms.

items.followUp: Write the subshell electronic configuration of the oxide ion, O²⁻.

rubric.why: These subshells account for the first ten electrons in the chloride ion.
rubric.description: Gives the configuration through the 2p subshell.

rubric.why: The remaining eight electrons fill the 3s and 3p subshells.

modelAnswer: A chlorine atom gains one electron to form Cl⁻, so the ion has 18 electrons.
The subshell electronic configuration of Cl⁻ is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶.

items.followUp: State two observations from Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Most alpha particles travelled through the foil with little or no deflection.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed through the foil undeflected or nearly undeflected.

rubric.why: A small number of alpha particles were deflected, and a very small number returned.
rubric.description: States that some particles were deflected or that a very few bounced back.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either observation about deflection or backscattering.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without being deflected.
Some alpha particles were deflected, and a very few bounced back.

items.followUp: Write any two physical properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Strong electrostatic attractions between ions generally give ionic compounds high melting points.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting points.

rubric.why: Ions can move and carry charge when an ionic compound is molten.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds generally have high melting points.
They conduct electricity when molten because their ions are free to move.

rubric.description: Writes the balanced reaction of magnesium with nitrogen.
